newsitem.title: PAKISTAN: Quake in Pakistan kills 60-year-old man.
newsitem.headline: Quake in Pakistan kills 60-year-old man.

text.p: An earthquake shook north and central Pakistan on Tuesday, killing at least one person, witnesses said.

An official at the Meteorology Department in the northwestern city of Peshawar said the epicentre of the quake, which measured 6.5 on the open-ended Richter scale, was about 250 km (156 miles) north of the city in the Hindu Kush mountain range.
Residents in the town of Muridke, north of Lahore, said a 60-year-old man had been killed when a house collapsed.
The quake, which occurred at 7.16 p.m. (1416 GMT) also jolted the capital Islamabad and the nearby city of Rawalpindi, residents said.
It was also felt in the Indian capital New Delhi, some 1,000 kms (600 miles) from the epicentre, but seismologists there said there were no immediate reports of injuries or damage.
An earthquake killed 1,560 people and injured 2,810 in eastern Iran on Saturday, according to a revised casualty toll given by a senior Iranian Interior Ministry official.
Previous official Iranian reports had said that about 2,400 people had died and 6,000 had been hurt.
